title: Handle untrusted text as data
summary: A workflow may receive text from a pull request. Do not paste untrusted text directly into a shell script; pass it as data and quote it.
introduction: A workflow may receive text from a pull request. Do not paste untrusted text directly into a shell script; pass it as data and quote it. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain handle untrusted text as data
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A workflow may receive text from a pull request. Do not paste untrusted text directly into a shell script; pass it as data and quote it.

blocks.code:
env:
  NOTE: A fixed practice message
steps:
  - run: printf "%s\n" "$NOTE"
blocks.title: Handle untrusted text as data

blocks.text: The shell prints the value as an argument. This fixed example teaches quoting without using attacker-controlled input.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why quote marks around $NOTE matter.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Never execute a message or title as if it were a trusted command.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub Actions further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/actions).
